scopes.label: One cell
scopes.note: Read one named cell. The ordinary getter still returns one row containing one value.

scopes.label: A rectangle
scopes.note: Read eight rows and three columns. The blank separator at row 18 stays in the result.

scopes.label: Part of one row
scopes.note: Read the first row inside the chosen rectangle. Zero means the first row of that rectangle.

scopes.label: Part of one column
scopes.note: Read the first column inside the chosen rectangle. This is a bounded eight-cell read.

scopes.label: A cell by row and column number
scopes.note: Read the same K13 cell using zero-based numbers: row 12 is Excel row 13, column 10 is K.

scopes.label: Several separate areas
scopes.note: The script reads two chosen rectangles and collects both results. The cells between them are not requested.

scopes.label: A whole tab’s used area
scopes.note: Ask the library how far the tab is used, then read that rectangle. Used areas can include cells with formatting but no values.

scopes.label: Every tab’s used area
scopes.note: The script goes through all six tabs and reads each used rectangle. This returns cell contents; charts, comments and formatting need separate reads.

methods.label: Values only
methods.why: See the numbers, text, dates and blanks currently held in the cells.
methods.assembly: The library returns the values in rows. No formula text is requested.

methods.label: Formulas only
methods.why: See the calculation written in each position. Cells without a formula return an empty string.
methods.assembly: The library returns the formulas in rows. It does not include their numerical results.

methods.label: Values and formulas — two lists
methods.why: Get both readings. The same position in each list refers to the same cell.
methods.assembly: Two library reads. The script puts them into one object with values and formulas fields.

methods.label: Value and formula together per cell
methods.api: range.values + range.formulas, joined by the script
methods.why: Read each address beside its current value and its formula, without matching up two separate lists.
methods.assembly: Two library reads. The script pairs matching positions and adds a cell address; this layout is made by the script.

methods.label: Formula details (advanced)
methods.why: Inspect the stored formula, the formula shown for the cell, and the library’s extra formula information. These getters are useful for spill or data-table cells.
methods.assembly: Three library reads, packaged by the script. This ordinary Summary example does not demonstrate a spill or a sensitivity table.

methods.label: Values and formula records through inspect
methods.why: Compare the other reading route: inspect returns a block of values and separate addressed formula records.
methods.assembly: The library creates these records. The capture explicitly saves its NDJSON and metadata; an inspection table here means a rectangle of cell values.

methods.label: Matching cells with value and formula
methods.why: Ask for cells matching some text. Each match already includes its address, value and formula.
methods.assembly: The library pairs value and formula for matching cells. This searches for selected cells; it does not read every cell in the area.

Twenty quarters, Q1 2023–Q4 2027. Fiscal year ends 31 December. Evidence cutoff 14 September 2026; latest actuals are H1 2026. No forecast replaces an already reported period.
AUM A / P&L E means the AUM quarter is disclosed but individual-quarter financial results are model estimates. H1 and FY earnings remain sourced actual controls. Forecast begins Q3 2026.

Core (company-adjusted) earnings remove non-core acquisition, restructuring and other adjustments, and eliminate consolidation gross-ups. Statutory profit and EPS are retained as historical memo inputs, not mixed into the forecast.
Use disclosed fee-paying AUM, excluding uncalled non-fee-paying commitments ($4.9bn at June 2026). Opening and closing AUM are stocks. Net flows and all earnings/costs are period flows.

A simple opening/closing midpoint assumes activity is spread through each quarter. It does not reproduce daily AUM or fund-level fee accrual. Historical fees are allocated by midpoint weights and reconcile to reported H1 and FY.

Model net management fees after distribution costs. Forecast applies 56bp, the reported 2025 average, to midpoint AUM with a quarter-year factor. Immaterial service income is absorbed in this blended rate. Historical gross fees and distribution costs are shown separately as memo lines.

The historical implied margin uses midpoint AUM and differs from the published margin. Base deliberately returns to the 2025 average 56bp despite H1 2026 average 52bp and 2025 exit run-rate 52bp. This is the exercise assumption; Downside tests continued 52bp.

Default allocation is Q1 10% / Q2 90% of H1, and Q3 10% / Q4 90% of FY less H1. These are explicit estimates, not disclosed quarter results. Forecast copies the corresponding allocated 2025 quarter. Changing allocation alters quarters but leaves historical H1/FY intact.

Fees depend on fund high-water marks, benchmarks, hurdles and crystallisation. The assumed AUM investment return is therefore not multiplied by an incentive rate to generate fees. Earned carry sits within performance fees where applicable. Acquired carry receivables are stocks and are not added to revenue.

H1 2026 statutory performance/pass-through fees contain a $19m gross-up, with $18m of associated compensation. Core metrics remove it; the model follows the reported core basis. No unsupported standalone carry or incentive-fee series is created.

All fixed compensation belongs to the recurring management-fee business. Forecast fixed compensation is $274m / 4 and other fixed costs including D&A $215m / 4. No inflation or incremental cost savings are assumed. Other employment expense stays $7m / 4.

Management participation is ($481m − $274m) / $1,077m. Performance/seed participation is $194m / ($281m + $38m). The latter attribution links fee costs to fees and seed costs to seed returns while preserving the company-reported total.

Servicing scales with average total AUM at the 2025 calibrated blended rate. The disclosed approximately 5bp excludes systematic long-only AUM; applying it to total group AUM would use the wrong denominator.

Seed investment gains and rental income stay at 2025 annual totals / 4. Management and seed financing remain $7m / 4 and $11m / 4. Management third-party profit share stays $2m / 4; performance share scales at $1m / $281m of fee revenue.

Model-defined core operating profit equals net revenue less core operating costs, including D&A and other employment costs. It is before net finance expense and third-party profit allocations. A separate operating-profit line excludes seed gains. Core PBT reconciles to the company.

Forecast tax is the unrounded 2025 ratio $86m / $407m. Forecast shares are 1,164.877368m. H1 actuals retain their reported rates and shares. Annual shares are day-weighted, and EPS equals total profit / weighted diluted shares; quarterly EPS is never added to make FY EPS.

2024 and 2025 FX totals are disclosed annually. Quarter FX is allocated in proportion to the reported other bucket after acquisitions; 2024 realisations are spread evenly. Residual other preserves each quarter total. n/d components remain in other, not assumed zero. Forecast FX, acquisitions, realisations and other are zero.

Change Assumptions D4: 1 Base; 2 Downside (zero flows, 52bp, half fees); 3 Upside (+2% flows, 58bp, 1.5× fees); 4 Zero PF (base AUM/margin, no forecast performance fees). Individual forecast quarters are editable. One engine recalculates every case.

Historical H1 2026 performance fees of $207m remain actual in every case. Only forecast performance fees become zero. FY2027 shows a full year without performance fees. Seed gains, their compensation and seed funding remain; Zero PF is not a zero-investment-income case.

AUM reconciles quarterly to source; fees, cost components, both PBT streams, tax, profit and weighted shares reconcile to H1/FY controls. EPS differences within 0.10 US cents reflect rounded published dollar profits and share counts. Allocation identities are labelled separately from source tie-outs.

Add the next quarter AUM bridge and next H1/FY financial control, preserve previous sources, replace affected forecast cells with allocation formulas, and move the forecast cutoff. Rebase exercise assumptions only deliberately; do not automatically substitute new management guidance.

Recalculated every case, confirmed historical invariance, tested a later-quarter driver and missing selected/unselected inputs, and inspected each sheet. Reopened the exported workbook to verify formulas, comments and outputs. Native Excel verification is recorded in the accompanying model record.
